title: Edge session reuse feedback-loop 5xx retrospective
body:
Summary:

On 2027-11-03 at ~09:12 UTC we observed a sharp wave of 5xx errors and streaming session chops for the Hosted API in eu-west-1. Impact lasted ~18 minutes with partial degradation for another 40 minutes. The outage surface was a mixed set: short-lived synchronous request 5xx spikes (~1.6k requests/s) and streaming clients experiencing repeated chunk drops and reconnects.

High level story: an edge optimization (session reuse + fewer TLS handshakes) combined with a new adaptive batching threshold and our edge->backend keepalive heuristics created a feedback loop. Under a transient traffic pattern (large fanout of short prefix requests from a customer test harness), many edge connections reused upstream backend connections that still had stale KV-cache state. When these reused sessions hit a code path that attempted aggressive adaptive batching, the backend rejected requests (502/503) while opening many short-lived retries; edge retry logic pushed bursts back to the cluster, forcing autoscaler reactions and exhausted connection pools on some backends. The combined effect created a transient storm of 5xx and streaming fragmentation.

Impact:
- Duration: full-severity 09:12:00 - 09:30:10 UTC; residual elevated errors and reconnects through 10:10 UTC.
- Customers affected: ~3% of active hosted-api customers in eu-west-1 saw elevated errors; 7 high-traffic customers reported streaming instability.
- Observable effect: 5xx rate from 0.03% baseline to 2.4% at peak; median p95 latency increased from 180ms to 1.1s for short text generation routes.
- Business impact: several customer support tickets; no known data loss.

Timeline (reconstructed from traces, edge logs, and oncall notes):
- 09:11:45 UTC: Canary metrics alert: hosted-api error rate exceeded threshold for eu-west-1 (alerts auto-created by SRE-alerts).
- 09:12:00 UTC: SRE pager oncall (Liam) acknowledged and opened triage Slack channel (#sre-incident-7890).
- 09:12:20 UTC: Initial dashboards show simultaneous increase in edge TLS session reuse ratio and backlog length on upstream connection pools.
- 09:13:10 UTC: Traces show increased retry attempts from edge -> backend (many 502/503 responses).
- 09:15:00 UTC: Streaming subsystem reports chunk sequencing gaps; several clients reconnecting with session reset.
- 09:16:30 UTC: Disable edge session reuse on eu-west-1 (feature toggle) as an emergency mitigation (Liam). 5xx rate fell but streaming issues continued.
- 09:20:00 UTC: Rollback adaptive batching threshold change that had been rolled out to eu-west-1 earlier that morning (Marina). Error rate drops further; streaming stabilizes gradually.
- 09:30:10 UTC: Incident declared mitigated for production traffic; follow-on stabilizations and customer-facing comms started.

Root cause (short):
- A recently deployed adaptive batching threshold tuning (rolled to eu-west-1 at 05:00 UTC) lowered the threshold that controls when the serving runtime aggregates concurrent small requests into a batch. In conjunction with an edge optimization that aggressively reused upstream keepalive connections, we created a scenario where multiple logically distinct requests were coalesced on the same backend connection while backend KV cache state for prefixes was stale. The backend code path attempted to fast-path some requests and returned 502/503. Edge retry and optimistic reuse amplified the failures into a short-lived cascade.

Contributing factors:
- Unsafe coupling between edge session reuse heuristic and backend connection semantics (keepalive + per-connection cache assumptions).
- Lack of a circuit-breaker tuned to this specific failure mode (we have generic breakers but they didn't trip fast enough under this pattern).
- Adaptive batching rollout had been accelerated without a rollback window coordinated with edge changes; both were live in eu-west-1 by morning traffic.
- Monitoring gap: the edge reuse ratio metric existed but no alert was tied to sudden changes with correlation to 5xx spikes.
- Oncall handoffs: morning shift had multiple open tasks; initial response delayed by ~2 minutes while noisy alerts were triaged.

Why this wasn't caught in staging:
- Traffic in staging does not emulate real customer prefix distributions and streaming multiplex patterns. The specific combination of short prefixes + high fanout came from customer test harness traffic we didn't mirror in canary.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Emergency toggle: disabled edge session reuse for eu-west-1 (rolled back 09:16:30 UTC).
- Rollback: reverted adaptive batching threshold change (rolled back 09:20:00 UTC).
- Rate dampening: adjusted edge retry jitter and backoff to be more conservative for 502/503 (temporary config).
- Autoscaler: temporarily increased min replicas for affected pool to absorb retries and reduce CPU pressure while we stabilized.

Longer-term fixes and action items (owners & ETA):
- [P0] Add an edge->backend connection semantics contract and tests (owner: Ravi Patel, ETA: 2027-12-01).
- [P0] Implement a targeted circuit-breaker that trips on rapid per-connection error amplification patterns (owner: Marina Chen, ETA: 2027-11-20).
- [P1] Rework adaptive batching rollout procedure to include a coordinated edge compatibility check and a mandatory canary workload that simulates short-prefix fanout (owner: Diego Alvarez, ETA: 2027-12-15).
- [P1] Add an alert which correlates edge reuse ratio delta with 5xx rate increase and triggers an automated mitigation runbook (owner: Aisha Khan, ETA: 2027-11-18).
- [P2] Improve streaming client telemetry to detect chunk sequencing gaps earlier and surface per-client hints to customer success (owner: Product-hosted-api; ETA: 2028-01-10).

Runbook updates (what changed in the ops playbook):
- New emergency knob documented: disable-edge-session-reuse regionally. Steps, rollback, and verification added.
- Incidents with combined edge reuse + batching symptoms should escalate to SRE lead immediately (new severity mapping).
- Added exact thresholds for when to pause autoscaler scale-up during backend error amplification (avoid scale-churn feedback).

Oncall notes / lessons learned (informal):
- Good: quick identification of edge->backend correlation using recently improved trace join keys.
- Bad: too many simultaneous changes in region (edge optimization + batching) without cross-team rollouts gating. We need a light process constraint: critical infra changes in the same region should require a short coordination window in the morning rollouts.
- Tip for next time: when seeing rising 5xx with increased reuse ratio, try toggling reuse heuristics first before scaling pools; scaling can sometimes make the retry storm worse.

Customer comms summary (for CSM):
- We experienced a transient service disruption in eu-west-1 affecting a subset of hosted-api traffic and streaming sessions for ~18 minutes with residual reconnects. Root cause: interaction between an edge connection reuse optimization and a recently changed adaptive batching threshold. We have reverted the risky changes, deployed safeguards, and are implementing longer-term fixes. Apology and offer for follow-up with impacted customers.

Open follow-ups (tracking):
- Postmortem writeup finalized and published to Confluence by 2027-11-10 (Aisha).
- Engineering change: PR for circuit-breaker (linked PR) needs review & merge; schedule post-merge canary (Marina).
- Customer outreach: coordinate with CS for top 7 affected customers; draft email and offer credit if requested (Diego).

Appendix: quick debug checklist used during the incident (copyable):
- Check edge reuse ratio (edge.metrics.session_reuse_ratio) and compare to 10-min baseline.
- Plot per-backend connection pool backlog and queue length.
- Check recent config/rollout events for adaptive batching and edge flags.
- Toggle reuse flag regionally and observe 2-min lag windows in metrics.
- If 502/503 persist after reuse toggle, rollback batching and reduce retry aggressiveness.

Slack/links: #sre-incident-7890, https://company.slack.com/archives/C0SRE/xyz, JIRA-RINF-7890, PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1842

Notes to future oncall: keep a small checklist pinned for edge-reuse style incidents (toggle, rollback, limit scale).

Document history:
- 2027-11-03: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2027-11-04: added timeline details and metrics (Liam)
- 2027-11-05: in_review updates and action items assigned (Marina)
